scope_note: Passive, non-intrusive inspection of HTTP response headers, cookies and TLS certificates. No exploitation, fuzzing, credential testing, port scanning or denial-of-service behaviour. Point it only at systems you own or have written permission to test.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy contains unsafe sources
findings.detail: 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval' keep inline or eval'd script executable, which defeats the purpose of the policy.
findings.remediation: Remove the unsafe keywords; whitelist exact origins, or use nonces/hashes for the few inline scripts the app needs.

findings.title: Target served over unencrypted HTTP
findings.detail: Content fetched from http://127.0.0.1:8080/bad-csp travels in plaintext: credentials, session cookies and page data are readable by anyone on the path.
findings.remediation: Serve the site over HTTPS only and redirect HTTP to HTTPS with 301.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options allows framing by any origin
findings.detail: ALLOWALL is a non-standard value that older browsers honour, leaving the page frameable.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.detail: Outbound requests can leak full URLs - which often carry tokens or identifiers - to third-party origins in the Referer header.
findings.remediation: Send: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or no-referrer for sensitive pages).

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options has an unexpected value
findings.detail: Only the exact token nosniff disables browser MIME sniffing.
findings.remediation: Set the header to exactly: nosniff

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.detail: Browser features such as camera, microphone and geolocation stay available to the document and its embeds.
findings.remediation: Send: Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() to disable features the app does not use.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
findings.detail: Without CSP the browser has no policy restricting script sources, so any injected markup executes as the page origin.
findings.remediation: Send a CSP that whitelists script sources, for example: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'.

findings.title: Target served over unencrypted HTTP
findings.detail: Content fetched from http://127.0.0.1:8080/insecure travels in plaintext: credentials, session cookies and page data are readable by anyone on the path.
findings.remediation: Serve the site over HTTPS only and redirect HTTP to HTTPS with 301.

findings.title: Clickjacking protection missing (X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors)
findings.detail: The page can be embedded by another origin, which is the basis of clickjacking attacks.
findings.remediation: Send: X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN); prefer CSP frame-ancestors 'none'.

findings.title: Cookie "tracking" is readable from JavaScript (no HttpOnly)
findings.detail: Without HttpOnly any cross-site scripting bug can exfiltrate or replace this cookie through document.cookie.
findings.remediation: Add the HttpOnly attribute to the cookie.

findings.title: Cookie "tracking" has no SameSite attribute
findings.detail: Browsers then apply their own default, which historically meant the cookie rode along on cross-site requests, enabling CSRF.
findings.remediation: Set SameSite=Lax for session cookies; use SameSite=None only when cross-site posting is genuinely required.

findings.title: Cookie "tracking" is missing the Secure flag
findings.detail: The page itself is served over plaintext http://, so this cookie crossed the network unencrypted and was readable by anyone on the path.
findings.remediation: Add the Secure attribute and serve the application over HTTPS only.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff missing
findings.detail: Browsers may MIME-sniff a response and execute it as a content type other than the one declared.
findings.remediation: Send: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.detail: Outbound requests can leak full URLs - which often carry tokens or identifiers - to third-party origins in the Referer header.
findings.remediation: Send: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or no-referrer for sensitive pages).

findings.title: X-Powered-By exposes the technology stack
findings.detail: Framework and runtime versions advertised in headers narrow down which known issues apply to this host.
findings.remediation: Disable the banner: Express app.disable('x-powered-by'); PHP expose_php = Off.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.detail: Browser features such as camera, microphone and geolocation stay available to the document and its embeds.
findings.remediation: Send: Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() to disable features the app does not use.

findings.title: Server header discloses a software version
findings.detail: A versioned product banner can be matched directly against public vulnerability and exploit data.
findings.remediation: Remove the version detail, leaving at most a generic product name. Nginx: server_tokens off; Apache: ServerTokens Prod.

findings.title: Target served over unencrypted HTTP
findings.detail: Content fetched from http://127.0.0.1:8080/ travels in plaintext: credentials, session cookies and page data are readable by anyone on the path.
findings.remediation: Serve the site over HTTPS only and redirect HTTP to HTTPS with 301.
